marks.gloss_en: רב הונא אמר מותר לטלטלו? והא רב הונא תלמיד דרב הוה, ורב כרבי יהודה סבירא ליה דאית ליה מוקצה! -- Rav Huna, Rav's student, should hold like his teacher, who follows R' Yehuda's muktze
but Rav Huna was Rav's student
במוקצה לאכילה סבר לה כרבי יהודה, במוקצה לטלטל סבר לה כרבי שמעון (= p_rav_kery_achila, p_rav_kershimon_tiltul) -- for moving, Rav follows R' Shimon, so Rav Huna's permission fits his teacher
in muktze for eating, he [Rav] holds like R' Yehuda
רב חסדא אמר אסור לטלטלו? והא רב יצחק בר אמי איקלע לבי רב חסדא... ואמר רב חסדא: חסרון כיס קא חזינן הכא! -- Rav Chisda had a duck's meat moved from sun to shade
שאני בר אווזא, דחזי לאומצא (= p_bar_avaza_chazi_leumtza) -- duck's meat is fit raw, unlike other unsalted meat
Rav Yitzchak bar Ami came to Rav Chisda's house and saw that duck's [meat] being moved from the sun to the shade
salted meat may be moved on Shabbat
salted fish may be moved
bones may be moved, because they are food for dogs
bundles of straw, bundles of wood and bundles of twigs: if he prepared them as animal food, they may be moved
רבן שמעון בן גמליאל -- הא דאמרן: RSBG [holds it], from what we said (the text does not say which statement; see header)
רבי שמעון -- דתנן: בני מלכים סכין על גבי מכותיהן שמן וורד... רבי שמעון אומר כל ישראל בני מלכים הם -- R' Shimon states it in the mishna
the mishna: princes may smear rose oil on their wounds
רבי ישמעאל ורבי עקיבא -- דתניא: ...תנא משום רבי ישמעאל ומשום רבי עקיבא כל ישראל ראויין לאותה איצטלא -- since all Israel are fit for a princely cloak, they hold all Israel are princes
one whose creditors claimed a thousand maneh of him, wearing a cloak worth a hundred maneh: he is stripped of it and dressed in a cloak fitting for him
אמר ליה רבי נתן: אלא מעתה חבילי זמורות יטלטלו מפני שהוא מאכל לפילין -- if being some animal's food suffices, bundles of vines should be movable as food for elephants!
ורבן שמעון בן גמליאל: נעמיות שכיחי, פילין לא שכיחי -- RSBG [would answer]: ostriches are common, elephants are not (= p_naamiyot_shechichi, p_pilin_lo_shechichi)
ostriches are common

אמר רב אשי לאמימר: אלא דקאמר ליה רבי נתן... חבילי זמורות יטלטל מפני שהוא מאכל לפילין -- אי אית ליה פילין אמאי לא? -- if owning the animal were the criterion, R' Natan's challenge would make no sense, for one who has elephants surely may move their food; so the criterion is suitability (= p_rav_ashi_raui)
Ameimar: and that is where he has ostriches
the mishna: nor [may one move] arum
all Israel are princes
the mishna: nor [may one move] first tithe [whose teruma was not taken]
דרחמנא אמר וצרת הכסף בידך, דבר שיש בו צורה -- second tithe is redeemed on something bearing a form, so an asimon does not redeem it (a verse-ground; svara stands in for דרחמנא אמר)
דרחמנא אמר ונתן הכסף וקם לו -- consecrated property is redeemed with money, so transferring it onto land does not redeem it (a verse-ground; svara stands in)
the mishna: nor [may one move] second tithe [and consecrated property that were not redeemed]
והא ההוא דאמר להו: מאן בעי קורניתא? ואישתכח חשי! -- a vendor called his wares koranita and they were chashei, so koranita is a known plant; the identification is replaced (אלא ... קורניתא חשי)
that man who said to them 'who wants koranita?' -- and it turned out to be chashei
bundles of sia, ezov and koranit: if he brought them in as firewood, he may not take from them on Shabbat
and he may pick [them] by hand and eat
and likewise with amita
the mishna: but [one may] not [clear away on Shabbat] tevel
